_what: How the Trillion Mac app carries and runs its programs on this Mac. At build time carry-computer-reader.sh copies `files` from `from` (the repository's one computer/ folder, never a copy) into the app's Contents/Resources/computer: a name lands at the same place (a file named from beside computer/, such as ../harness or ../parts/live-namespace, lands at the same place beside it, so every import resolves as in the repository), and a row { from, to } lands at `to` instead (computer/'s installed node_modules goes beside computer/, so modules carried from harness/, src/ and parts/ find their packages too). It puts `runtime` (Node.js, MIT licence, its LICENSE carried beside the files) at Contents/MacOS/node and signs it with the app's own identity. This file is carried as Contents/Resources/computer-reader.json. `children` are the programs the app runs as its own child processes on that runtime, so macOS gives each the app's permissions and the person turns on one switch named Trillion: each row's `entry` (relative to computer/), its `args`, and how it restarts after it stops (`restart_seconds`: the first wait, the longest, and how long a run must last before the wait starts again from the first). Every child gets the account key on standard input (its first line), never on a command line, in a file or in a log. Every child ends once the app that started it is gone (computer/end-with-the-app.mjs), so a crashed or replaced app never leaves its programs running beside the new app's. The reader (computer/read-this-computer.mjs --keep-reading) and the connections helper (computer/carry-connections.mjs) are no longer rows here: the helper starts them as its own children, by what the account has installed (computer/program-host.mjs, recipes in computer/mac-tools.json `programs`), and both run as before while no starting set is installed or the account cannot be read. The reader reads this computer's places; the camera receiver takes the clips a camera on this Mac's network pushes over FTP and sends them into the person's files (parts/receive-files-over-ftp); the camera stream receiver takes a camera's live stream at the one address its rows give it and sends it where the person's Camera streams row says (parts/receive-a-camera-stream); the connections helper carries iMessage and other connections only this computer reaches; the helper (harness/wake-sessions.mjs) keeps this computer's AI sessions reachable and runs the Mac's own tools (computer/mac-tools.mjs, placement:your-computer), skipping the reader the app already runs. The browser offers row (extension/native-host/offer-in-browsers.mjs offer) is a short pass, not a program that keeps running: it offers Trillion's extension in each installed browser once and places the browser native messaging host manifests (unless the person removed them), then ends, and its restart wait runs it again every six hours. Adding a program is a row here. The App Store build is sandboxed and carries and starts none of them.

environment._what: Set on every program the app starts (and so on everything those programs start). The app is signed and its Contents is sealed: a file written inside it breaks the seal and macOS then reads the installed app as damaged. Python writes a compiled copy of every module a program imports (computer/resident.py) beside it unless told not to, which on 2026-10-07 added Contents/Resources/computer/__pycache__ to an installed release.

carried_code._what: The carried-code check (F-0245, F-0617). carry-computer-reader.sh runs carried-code-manifest.mjs after the carry, which writes Contents/Resources/`manifest` (every file under the carried roots and each `also` file with its BLAKE3 identity, compiled code by its signature) and puts the manifest's own BLAKE3 identity in the app's Info.plist under `info_key`, which the app's code signature binds. Before any program starts, App/CarriedCode.swift checks the app's own signature, the manifest against that identity, every listed file (bytes, signature or link) and that no other file was added under a root, and that the program's entry is a listed file. Before a program starts only its entry is checked (its bytes; the kernel checks a native entry's signature); the whole check runs once per installed build after the first start, and its pass is kept at Application Support/`checked_record` by the app's CDHash and manifest identity, so a launch of a checked build walks nothing (CarriedCode.swift invariant 4). On any difference nothing starts and the menu bar panel shows `words.reinstall` until Trillion is installed again. `environment_removed` is taken off every program's environment, so a variable set for the whole login session cannot make the carried runtime load code from outside the app.

words.reinstall: Trillion's own files on this Mac were changed after it was installed, so it is not running them. Download Trillion again from {gateway}/download/Trillion.dmg and replace the app.

app._event_rows: Every line this app keeps about this computer (its own events, every line the engine writes on its standard error, its children's output), each a row of the person's list `list` (labelled `label`, rows of `row_type`), written through the account's own records write (App/ComputerEventRows.swift). Never a file on this computer (the person: every note, record, event and check is a row in his Trillion lists). The rows of this computer are numbered in order. A write that adds rows removes, in the same write, the ones that fell `most_rows` behind, so the list keeps this computer's newest `most_rows` lines (the old engine.log kept 4 files of 4 MiB at 2048-byte lines: 8192 lines). A line longer than `most_line_bytes` is cut there and marked. Lines wait in memory until the account can take them, at most `most_waiting`. Past that the oldest goes, and the next row says how many went (`dropped`). At most `batch_rows` rows are written at a time, `flush_seconds` after the first one waits. The startup decoder only adds meaning to the lines it knows; no line is dropped for being unknown.

local_runtime._what: A build may carry one explicitly prepared local runtime package into Contents/Resources/local-runtime. It is copied only when TRILLION_LOCAL_RUNTIME_PACKAGE names a completed package; user startup never rebuilds it. A finalized signed native artifact is carried only from an explicit pinned build input. The engine's product settings (word, hosts, secret home, tools source, the hosting app's report) are the app's own file computer/product-settings.json, carried like every other file of this list to product_settings; ComputerReader names that sealed file in the engine's launch setting PRODUCT_SETTINGS, overriding inherited values. A native build also supplies the engine's host-events declaration (TRILLION_NATIVE_HOST_EVENTS with its BLAKE3 and byte pin), carried to host_events: the host event kinds the app observes and sends the engine. The app starts the selected runtime with its private per-user adoption descriptor; package files are covered by the carried-code manifest and app signature.
